newsitem.title: USA: Norfolk says Conrail ignores fiduciary duty.
newsitem.headline: Norfolk says Conrail ignores fiduciary duty.

text.p: Norfolk Southern Co said on Wednesday that Conrail Inc's board of directors was continuing to ignore its fiduciary duty in rejecting a takeover bid from Norfolk Southern.
Earlier on Wednesday, Conrail said it was recommending that shareholders not tender their shares to Norfolk Southern, which has offered to buy the railroad for $10 billion.
Instead, Conrail and CSX Corp reaffirmed their $8.5 billion merger agreement and said they have been discussing increasing the value of the pact upon consummation of the transaction.
Conrail has repeatedly said that the CSX transaction provided more strategic benefits.

"The Conrail board continues to ignore its fiduciary duty to shareholders," Norfolk Southern said. "The CSX proposal is not a 'strategic combination,' but a strategy to subvert the intent of state law and coerce Conrail shareholders into accepting an inadequate offer for their shares."
Norfolk said the CSX proposal required Conrail shareholders wait an indeterminate length of time for regulatory merger approval, for an unknown return on 60 percent of the shares outstanding.
Conrail and CSX said earlier there was no assurance their pact would be modified.
